# A group header cell drags its whole group

## Context

The operator's manual test of `examples/grid/headerGroups` (2026-11-08 23:57) blocks the 13.4 release, in part because "top-level headers can not get dragged … this is not cool for a new demo." #20379 shipped header groups with "Dragging a whole group" explicitly out of scope. The demo now needs it.

## The Problem

A grid with groups lets you reorder the months inside Q3, but you can't move Q3 itself. In the recording, the gesture on a group cell selects its text instead of moving anything.

## The Architectural Reality

- Design authority: the operator's input above (2026-11-08) adds the gesture. #20379's rules still hold: a leaf never leaves its group, and a drop never splits a group across regions.
- The group row is a projection. `grid.header.GroupRow` cells are placed from their leaves' `columnPositions` and owned by `grid.header.Wrapper`. A leaf reorder runs through `draggable/grid/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs` on the leaf row, and the group row re-projects after it.
- A group's leaves are contiguous in the `columns` collection, so moving a group means moving one contiguous run of leaves.

## The Fix

The shape is for the owner. Dragging a group cell moves its whole run of leaves to a new position among the region's top-level units: other groups and ungrouped columns. It never lands inside another group. The drag shows the group as one proxy, and the group row and the leaf row re-project once on drop.

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Dragging `Q3` before `Q2` in `examples/grid/headerGroups` moves Jul, Aug and Sep as one block. The group row shows Q1, Q3, Q2, Q4, and every group cell's edges match its leaves (e2e, DOM rects).
- [ ] A group drag never lands inside another group, and never moves a group to another region.
- [ ] Ungrouped columns move around groups as before, and leaf reorder inside a group is unchanged (e2e).
- [ ] The operator's manual pass on `examples/grid/headerGroups` accepts the gesture.

## Out of Scope

- More than one group level.
- Collapsing a group, and sorting or menus on a group cell.
- A leaf leaving its group (#20379).

- 2026-11-09T00:03:20Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `2003146` - "fix(grid): a group drag keeps a scrolled header and survives a pending start (#20627)

In a scrolled grid the group row lost its scroll twice:
- A re-projection replaced the part's id-less track. A resize, every column-resize sample and a group drag's press all re-project.
- A group drop reorders the cells. DeltaUpdates' layout heal then toggles their parent's display and restores only that parent's own scroll, not the scroll of the part above the track.

Either way the centre part clamped to 0. The release then mapped against 0, and the cells sat apart from their leaves. The track now carries an id and only spans the scroll extent. The cells sit in the part itself, whose scroll the heal keeps.

The drag zone is now created once the row projects draggable cells, and registered under the row. Escape therefore reaches it from a gesture's first frame. A release or cancel during the pending start waits for that start, so no proxy or dragging row is left behind, and a pending Escape moves nothing."
- 2026-11-09T00:17:05Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `12832c0` - "fix(grid): group cells turn draggable only once their drag zone is registered (#20627)

While the drag zone's module was still loading, the group cells already rendered as `neo-draggable`. A gesture could start with no zone for the main thread to resolve, so its Escape had no owner and the release still moved the group.

`createDragZone` now awaits the zone's registration with the main thread, then re-projects. Only from then on does `project` mark the cells draggable."

* feat(grid): a group header cell drags its whole group (#20627)

A group cell is now a drag source while its region's toolbar is
dragResortable. The drop moves the group's contiguous run of leaves as one
block among the region's top-level units (the other groups and the ungrouped
columns), at the slot between the units whose centres straddle the release,
so a group never lands inside another one and never leaves its region. The
proxy is the cell itself, held to its region's part of the row; it takes the
cell's look outside the row and carries its label as the proxy component's
own text config, which otherwise resets the cloned root text. The cells no
longer select their text on a drag.

The commit is the existing column path: columns.move() per leaf, then
grid.Container#onColumnsMutate once, and Toolbar#measureAfterUpdate, so the
group row projects from positions measured after the buttons rendered in
their new order (projecting before that reads every leaf's old x).
GroupRow.getUnits now builds both the projection's cells and the drop's
units.

* fix(grid): a group drag keeps a scrolled header and survives a pending start (#20627)

In a scrolled grid the group row lost its scroll twice:
- A re-projection replaced the part's id-less track. A resize, every column-resize sample and a group drag's press all re-project.
- A group drop reorders the cells. DeltaUpdates' layout heal then toggles their parent's display and restores only that parent's own scroll, not the scroll of the part above the track.

Either way the centre part clamped to 0. The release then mapped against 0, and the cells sat apart from their leaves. The track now carries an id and only spans the scroll extent. The cells sit in the part itself, whose scroll the heal keeps.

The drag zone is now created once the row projects draggable cells, and registered under the row. Escape therefore reaches it from a gesture's first frame. A release or cancel during the pending start waits for that start, so no proxy or dragging row is left behind, and a pending Escape moves nothing.

* fix(grid): group cells turn draggable only once their drag zone is registered (#20627)

While the drag zone's module was still loading, the group cells already rendered as `neo-draggable`. A gesture could start with no zone for the main thread to resolve, so its Escape had no owner and the release still moved the group.

`createDragZone` now awaits the zone's registration with the main thread, then re-projects. Only from then on does `project` mark the cells draggable."
